Vice-Admiral, Vice-Chief of Naval Staff Board; b. in '66 in Tokyo; graduated from the Naval Academy '86 and then the Naval College '97; Navigating-Lieutenant of the transport Saikyo Maru during the Japan-China War; Captain '05; Chief of Staff to the 4th Squadron during the Russo-Japanese War; Rear-Admiral '09; Chief of the Bureau of Personnel '09-13; Pres. of Naval College '13-14; Com. of 1st Fleet Aug., '14 and partook in the war, then transferred to Com. of 3rd Flotilla Feb., '15; present post Dec., '15. Add. Hommura, Azabu, Tokyo.

Treasurer, Imp. Household; b. in '68 at Saga; grad. from Imp. Tokyo Univ. (Law) '96, and at the same time passed the higher civil service exam.; Tax Inspector '97 attached to Nagasaki Taxation Office; transferred to Finance Office to be made its Sec. '00; Dir. of Finance Bur., then Debt Bur. Add. Yoyohata, near Tokyo.

Count, Mem. House of Peers, Mem. of Japanese Census Commission, Consulting Statist to the Cabinet, Mem. of International Statistical Society, Hon. Mem. of Royal Statistic Society (England), etc.; b. '70 in Echigo, son of Lord Mitsu-aki, scion of the House of Yanagisawa which hereditarily held the fief of Koriyama, Yamato; adopted '86 as son and heir of the main house, and succeeded to the title '93; grad. at the Peers' College with honour '94; sent by the Imperial Court to Germany for study and attended the Universities of Berlin, Vienna, Strassburg, Brussels and Paris, studying statistics; meanwhile appointed on the suite of H.H. Prince Kan-in who was sent to attend the Diamond Jubilee of Emperor Francis Joseph; returned home in '00; attended the International Statistical Conference six times as representative of Japan, from that at Christiania in '99 to the latest at the Hague '11. He held Presidency of the 1st Mutual Insurance Co. till '15, and is now its adviser. Add. Tamachi Hatchome, Shiba, Tokyo.

Paymaster-Lieut. (ret.), Vice-Gov. of Hypothec Bank of Japan; b. in '67 in Nagasaki-ken; graduated from the College of Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ., '90. Entered the Bank of Japan immediately after graduation; travelled Europe in '96; was appointed Chief of the Issue Dep't, Auditor to the New York Agency, Chief of the National Loan Bureau; resigned '13, and appointed Dir. of the Hypothec Bank; present post '13. Add. Harajuku, Tokyo.

Dir. of Kinjo Middle School, author, and retired diplomat; b. '50 in Oita-prefecture; graduated from the Keiogijuku, '70; entered the central Government as Secretary to the Treasury, '78; resigned with Count Okuma in '81 and took charge of the Hochi Shimbun, in company with the late Mokichi Fujita; took part in the formation of the Kaishinto (Progressive party); made tour in Europe and America, '86-88; Master of Ceremonies and Chief of the Bureau of Imperial Tombs, '90-96; Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to China, '97-98; placed on the retired list in '99. He has written "Keikoku Bidan" (story of ancient Greece), "Ukishiro Monogatari" (a marine novel); "News Society," etc. Add. Harajuku, Tokyo.

Pres. and Mng.-Dir. of the 1st Mutual Life Insur. Co., was b. '65 in Okayama; grad. the Third Higher School in '89; entered the Japan Life Insur. Co., and in '93 was made manager of the Kyosai Life Insur. Co.; went over to Belgium to attend the International Congress of Actuaries held in Sept. '95; and afterward entered a German Life Insur. Co. to receive its business training; was appointed an official in the Dep't of Agr. and Com., but soon resigned to start the present Co. Add. Omori, near Tokyo.

Vice-Adm., Com. of the 2nd Fleet; b. '60 in Aichi-ken; Naval Ensign in '85, and repeatedly promoted was elevated to Captain in '01 and finally to the present rank. Long served as Staff-Officer of the Standing Squadron, then Attache to the Legation at Petrograd, and Vice-Com. of the Yashima, commanding the Asama in Russo-Japanese War; Dir. of Naval Staff College '12-13; Com. of Maizuru Admiralty '13-14; Minister of Navy '14-15, present post Dec. '15. Add. Navy Office.

Manager of the Shibusawa's Office, Dir. of the Shinagawa Fire Brick Co., Shibusawa Warehouse Co. etc., was b. '73 in Uwajima, Iyo; grad. Tokyo Higher Commercial School in '94; appointed Per. Sec. to Baron Shibusawa. He travelled once in Europe and America with the Baron. Add. Shirokane-Daimachi, Shiba, Tokyo.

a millionaire who sprang from obscurity to the present affluence, greatest perhaps next to the Mitsui and the Mitsubishi; b. '38 in Toyama-ken; and was an apprentice at a shop in Tokyo and finally opened an exchange shop on his own account. This was enlarged in scope and developed into a bank. He has founded several other banks and has moreover lent his powerful banking in the starting of the Tokyo Fire Insurance Co., the Imp. Marine Insurance Co. and Kyosai Life Insurance Co. Being a public-spirited man he does not spare to furnish fund to any useful undertakings. The fund required in the Osaka Harbour Works was almost wholly supplied by him. He is a business man of extraordinary integrity and diligence; is Mem. of House of Peers. Add. Yokoami-cho, Honjo, Tokyo.

Member of Privy Council since 1916, was b. '59 in Fukuoka-ken. Grad. the Keiogijuku, the Chuô Shoin at Hongkong and finally from Cambridge Univ. in England; Prof. in the 3rd Higher Sch. in '89; Secretary to the Cabinet; Councillor to the Legislation Bureau; Director of General Education Bureau in '97; Chief Secretary to the Cabinet '98; Member of House of Peers from '00 to '16; Vice-Min. of the Dep't of Agr. and Com. in '01, resigned in '11. Add. Sadowaracho, Ushigome, Tokyo.

highest tax-payer, mine-owner, Dir. of several Cos.; b. '49 in Chikuzen; studied at the Keiogijuku '72; has made a fortune in coal-mining; founded single-handed the Meiji Semmon College in 1908 by contributing 3,000,000 yen, and has been rewarded for it with 3rd class of the Sacred Treasure. Add. Wakamatsu, Fukuoka.

Lieut.-Gen. (ret. '14), ex-Commander of the 11th Division; b. '53 at Kyoto; Sub-Lieut.; studied in France '86-90; Major '92 and instructor at the Cadet School; Col. '97 and Dir. of Toyama Military School till '03; Major-Gen. '03 and took part in Russo-Japanese War as Com. of the 4th Brigade, Infantry; Lieut.-Gen. '10. Add. Nishinada, Hyogo-ken.

Dr. Agr., Prof. at Agr. Coll., Imp. Tokyo Univ. and Pres. of Tokyo Agr. Univ. (private); b. 60 in Kumamoto; grad. from above Coll. '83; studied in Germany '99-02; Expert to the Agr. and Com. Dep't; Prof. in '94. Add. Aoyama Minamicho, Tokyo.

D.C.L. (Japan), Judge of Supreme Court since '01; b. '62 in Nagano-ken; grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ., class '88; sat at Tokyo, Chiba and Hakodate District Courts, and Tokyo and Hakodate Appeal Courts before his transfer to the present post; teaches at the Waseda Univ., being an authority on claims; was sent abroad on official mission '09. Add. Nakano, near Tokyo.

Baron, (cr, '15), Pres. of the Supreme Court since '06 ; was b. '50 in Oita-ken ; entered the judicial service '76, Public Procurator '80, the acting Dir. of Criminal Bureau and Sec. of the Dep't which post he resigned to study law in Europe '86-91 ; was appointed on return Pub. Proc. of the Tokyo Appeal Court, Councillor, then Vice-Min. of Justice '96, Proc.-Gen. '98, Chief Pub. Proc. of Tokyo Appeal Court '99. Add. Kagurazaka, Ushigome, Tokyo.

Geologist, D. Sc. (Japan), Prof. in the Imp. Tokyo Univ. ; was b. '60 in Nagasaki ; grad. Geology in the Imp. Tokyo Univ. and was subsequently appointed an official at the Dep't of Agr. and Com. in '82 ; sent to Germany to prosecute further study in '86 ; appointed Prof. at his alma mater on returning home. Add. Higashi-Goken-cho, Ushigome, Tokyo.

veterinarian, principal and proprietor of the Azabu Veterinary School ; was b. '61 in Kagoshima ; studied veterinary science at the Agr. Col., Imp. Tokyo Univ., and further in America ; appointed Prof. in the Agr. Col. of the Imp. Tokyo Univ. '87, which he resigned some years ago to start his own veterinary school in Tokyo. Add. Sanko-cho, Shirokane, Tokyo.

Prop. of the Yonei Firm, Dir. of the Meiji Gum Co., the Kirin Beer Brewing Co., etc. ; was b. '61 in Okayama-ken ; grad. the Keiogijuku ; then entered the business circle and established an import business at Ginza, the "Yonei Shoten." Add. Kaminibancho, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. of Kobe Marine, Transport and Fire Ins. Co., and of Nisshin Fire and Marine Ins. Co., b '66 in Ishikawa-ken ; became a lawyer '87 ; elected Vice-Chairman of Osaka Lawyer's Association '99 ; gave up the profession and became Mng.-Dir. of Kobe Marine Ins. Co. '07 ; organized Nisshin Co. '11. Add. Kyomachi Hondori, Nishi, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir. of Mitsui Bank, was b. '68 at Numazu ; studied in America '90-95, and entered the Nippon R'ly Co., removed to the Mitsui Bank which sent him abroad '00 to inspect banking business '02 ; Chief of the Yokohama Branch 1903 and next that at Osaka '08 ; Mng.-Dir. '10. Add. Aoyama Minami-cho, Tokyo.

Maj.-Gen., Dir. of Remounting Dep't ; was b. '68 in Oita ; Sub-Lieut., cavalry '88 ; held posts of Prof. at Staff Coll., Chief Staff at 7th Div., Dir. of Riding School, Com. of 2nd Cavalry Brigade, etc. Add. Meguro, near Tokyo.
Chief of Police Bureau, Household Dep't, was b. '45 in Ishikawa ; held local posts at Kagoshima etc. ; Dir. Finance Bureau, Imp. Household. Add. Shimonibancho, Tokyo.
Pres. of 7th High School, b. '70 in Ishikawa ; grad. from Philosophy, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '97 ; was Dir. of Middle Schools, Prof. at Waseda, etc. Add. Kagoshima.

ex-Minister to Siam ; b. '59 in Kumamoto-ken, attaché in '86, appointed to The Hague Legation in '88, Per. Sec. to Minister of Education in '93 and then Prof. in Third High School, 2nd Legation Sec. at Vienna in '98, removed to The Hague in '00, and transferred to Vienna in '01 till '04 ; Minister to Siam in '08, relieved in '14. Add. Foreign Office.

Dr. Lit. (Japan), historian and historiographer, Prof. at Waseda University ; b. '64, Niigata ; wrote on historical subjects to the Yomiuri and completed "The Dictionary of Japanese Geography" in '09 after 16 years work ; "The Reverse History of Japan" (with pyramidal for basis modern time and summit for ancient time) in '14. Add. Yarai, Ushigome, Tokyo.

Per. Sec. to Foreign Minister since '96 and attaché at the Board of Ceremonies, Imp. Court, b. '50 ; clerk at Foreign Office in '77–86, attache in '87, élève Consul at Manila in '92 and then attaché in Berlin. Add. Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Pres. of the Oriental Development Co., b. '64 in Chiba-ken ; appointed a Secretary of the House of Representatives, '90 ; then Secretary in prefectural Government of Saitama, Osaka and Aichi, Governor of Kagawa-ken. Director of Local Administration Bureau, Home Office '03 ; Vice-Minister of Home Affairs in Jan. '06, Vice-Pres., Oriental Development Co., Seoul in '08. Add. Seoul, Korea.
Commander (ret.), 2nd Count, Mem. House of Peers, Pre. Japan Lifeboat Asso., was b. '55 ; studied in England, and then grad. from Naval Cadet School in '80. Add. Sagacho, Fukagawa, Tokyo.

Dir. of the Bank of Japan, was b. '63 in Kagoshima. Early entered the Bank of Japan in which he has gradually distinguished himself to be given an important position of its Director. Add. Kita-igacho, Yotsuya, Tokyo.

Count (cr. Vis. '96 and Count '07), Vice-President of Privy Council since '12 ; b. '41 at Tokushima ; entered the civil service early in the Meiji era and after having held various posts in the Treasury, Home Office and elsewhere was appointed the Gov. of Tokyo-fu and then Vice-Min. of Home Affairs. Then began his Ministerial career, first as Minister of Edu., '90 ; Justice, '91-96 ; Home Affairs, '93-96 ; Communications, twice '98-00 and '01-3 ; Home Affairs '04, which last he had to resign in connection with the Sept.-5th-'05 anti-Peace Agitation in Tokyo. Add. Miyamura-cho, Azabu, Tokyo.

Vice-Adm., Com.-in-Chief of 1st Fleet; b. '59 in Kochi-ken ; appointed Sub-Lieut. in '83 ; was at one time Staff Officer of the Kure Adm., Chief of the First Bureau, Chief Staff Office of Sasebo Adm., Com. of the Naniwa and Takasago, and some others, Rear-Adm. in '07, Vice-Adm. '09 ; Pres. of Naval Staff Col. in '10 ; Com. of 2nd Squad. in '11-12, Chief of Edu. Board '12-14 ; Com. of the Kure Adm. '14-15. Add. Navy Office.
Pres. of 5th High School ; b. '76 in Yamaguchi ; grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '99 ; was Prof. at 2nd High School, School Inspector, etc. Add. Kumamoto.

millionaire dealer in iron and copper and importer and exporter in Kyoto, b. in Kanazawa '77, brother of Mr. S. Hayakawa, banker, and was adopted by the Yuasa of Kyoto ; grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '91. Add. Takakura Higashi-iru, Gojodori, Kyoto.

Gov. of Shizuoka since 1914 ; b. '74 in Fukushima ; grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '93 ; held posts of secretary at Shiga, Hyogo and other provinces ; then Secretary and Dir. of Local Government Bureau, Home Office, and Gov. of Okayama. Add. Shizuoka.

general exporter and importer in Kobe, Aud. of Masuda Flour Mill Co. and Mem. of Kobe Chamber of Commerce; b. '69 in Wakayama-ken; was Mng. of the well-known Masuda Firm. Add. Yamamoto-dori Gochome, Kobe.

Vice-Min. of Communications since '14; was b. '65 in Shizuoka; grad. Law Coll., Imp. Univ. '93, and has been connected with the Dep't ever since, having been Secretary, Dir. of Maritime Bureau, etc. Add. Nakarokubanch, Kojimachi, Tokyo.

Dir. of Imp. Music Academy since '08; b. '63 in Saga; first studied Medicine at Imp. Tokyo Univ., but left it unfinished in '84; held posts of Prof. at various Gov. Schools, Dir. of Middle Schools, etc. Add. Ichigaya, Ushigome, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen., Com. of 15th Division; b. in Kochi-ken; Sub-Lt., '82; graduated from Military Staff College; studied in England, Vice-Chief of Gen. Staff of 2nd Army in Russo-Japanese War; Com. of 27th Brigade '09; Sec. Chief of General Staff till '14, when transferred to Dir. of Mil. Staff College; present post in Jan. '15. Add. Toyohashi.

Prop. and Edit. of the Herald of Asia, started by him in '16, an English weekly review of life and progress in the Orient; b. '62 in Hoki Province, and grad. Sapporo Agrl Col. '84; was long on the staff of the Japan Mail; entered civil service for a short while and was twice appointed Per. Sec. to the late Prince Ito when he was Premier; frequently visited Europe and America; was during the Russo-Japanese War a resident correspondent of the London Standard in Tokyo, accompanied the late Prince Ito to Seoul as non-official mem. of the Residency-Gen., and in January '06 he took over the Seoul Press formerly owned by an Englishman. Withdrew from it in '09, to start the Oriental Information Agency in New York City. Returned to Tokyo in December '10 to assume the control of the Japan Times, from which withdrew in '14. Made a tour to U.S.A. with Baron Shibusawa in '15. Add. Hommuracho, Azabu, Tokyo.

Director of the Taiwan Sugar Co., was b. '54 at Kagoshima; studied at an American Col. '73-79; Sec. of the former Public Works Dep't '79; transferred to the R'ly Bureau '83 and remained in the service as Dep't Dir. till '09 when he was placed on retired list. Add. Ochiai-mura, near Tokyo.

—Founded 1831; publishes a monthly organ Dai Nippon Nokai-ho, and maintains Tokyo Agricultural University (private) in Tokyo as its educational institution. Tameike, Akasaka, Tokyo.

—Pioneer association of the kind in Japan and was est. about 1880 by the late Sir Earnest Satow and others in Japan for studying and investigating Japanese customs, history, literature, etc. List of members 350 including residing abroad. Keio University, Tokyo.

—Founded 1900; funds ¥150,000 to be created. Subscription in proportion to the capital paid up of the associated banks, ranging from ¥200 to ¥1,000. The members number 69 banks. Pres. Baron E. —Founded June, 1896; issues a monthly periodical; members numbered 1,700 at the end of Feb., 1916. Dues, ordinary membership 20 sen per month. Directors Y. Ishiyama, S. Ikeda, K. Harada, T. Hanai, etc. Add. Nishi-Hibiya, Kojimachi, Tokyo.
—Founded 1882; publishes a monthly, Botanical Magazine. Dues ¥3.60 per annum. Members number 400. Pres. Dr. J. Matsumura; Chief Dir. Dr. K. Shibata. Add. Botanical Garden, Tokyo.

Founded 1878; dues for regular member ¥5 per annum, associate ¥3, these numbering 650 in all. Publishes a monthly Tokyo Kwagakukwaishi. Pres. U. Suzuki; Secy. Y. Shibata, K. Aso. Add. Science College, Imp. University, Tokyo.

Pres. Dr. W. Watanabe. Add. Kagacho, Kyobashi, Tokyo.

Yokoyamacho, Nihombashi, Tokyo. Manufacturers of and dealers in hair brushes; have a factory at Koishikawa, Shibuya and Tamagawa; annual output is estimated at ¥100. Prop. Y. Tokunaga.
Kyobashiku, Tokyo. Est. 1897; cap. ¥1,875 p.u.; res. 1,040; div. 15%. Pres. K. Yamada; Mng.-Dirs. S. Asano, K. Okura, S. Fukayama.
Kawasaki, Kanagawa-ken. Est. Apl. 1876; cap. ¥2,600 p.u.; manufacture electric lamps etc. Pres. I. Fujioka.
Azumamachi, Tokyo-fu. Est. 1901; cap. ¥225 p.u.; res. ¥24; div. 8%. Mng.-Dir. N. Nagatomi; Dirs. H. Okawa, M. Onishi, K. Kimura, E. Tanaka.
Nakamura-cho Yokohama. Est. '90; exporters of nursery stocks, seed and plants; capital ¥500. Branches: London New York, etc. Directors. U. Suzuki (Mng.-Dir.), S. Iida (Mng.)

Osaka, general exporters and importers; line of exports,—general Japanese produce, drugs, oils, chemicals, manufactured goods etc.; line of imports,—chemicals, dyes, drugs etc.; branches at Kobe, Kyoto and Tokyo, and London office 65 Fenchurch St., E.C. Pres., D. Nagase, Dojima Hama-dori, Osaka.

Hirano-cho, Kobe. Formed 1868 by E. H. Hunter; first engaged in rice export business but have begun many years since to import machineries and also engaged in antimony refining business; have special connection with Osaka Iron Works. Prop. Ryutaro Hunter.

Nakanoshima, Osaka. Est. 1905 as partnership firm with capital ¥1,000; manufacturers and exporters of underwear, etc., annual export amounting to ¥4,000, also manufacture and export yarns to China and India; branches at Kobe and Tsingtau. Acting partner, Y. Kitagawa.
Masagocho, Yokohama. Leading silk exporters, est. '99 with capital ¥100 p.u. Brand: Kawamata Habutaye, Deer brand. Mng.-Dir. K. Komatsu.
Newchwang, Manchuria. Oil factors and shipping agents. Branches: London, Dairen, Kobe, Tokyo, Vladivostock, Mukden, Harbin, etc. Prop. Sokichi Kodera, Nakayamatedori, Kobe.

Importers and dealers in groceries, provisions and agents of Kirin Beer, Nunobiki Tansan Mineral Water, Jas. Buchanan's Whisky, J. Brown's Scotch Whisky, etc. Head Office; Honcho, Yokohama. Est. 1885 by late Mr. H. Isono, reorganized as partnership unlimited company 1903; changed into limited liability company May '11. Warranted purveyors to the Imperial Household and the Imperial Navy. Capital ¥500. Branches: Tokyo, Osaka, Kobe, Moji and Seoul. Directors: G. Yonei (Pres.), C. Isono (Vice-Pres.), M. Miyaji (Mng. Dir.), K. Sano (Dir.).

Honcho, Yokohama. Importers and exporters; est. Feb. '12; Cap. ¥500. Principal exports,—Timber, sulphur, superphosphates, spelter, metals and minerals, Portland cement, fish-oil, sugar, flour, etc.; principal imports,—sugar, grains, sulphate of ammonia, iron, steel, hides and skins, etc. Branches: Tokyo, Kobe, Osaka, Sydney, Shanghai, Dairen, Hankow, Tientsin, Tsingtau, Tainan, Takao. Nawa, Shimonoseki, Otaru, Nagoya, Newchwang, and London. Have flour mills, of flour, sugar refinery, etc., also possess Matsuo sulphur mine. Dirs. Fusajiro Nakamura and Masutaro Masuda.

General importers and exporters, Surugacho, Nihombashi, Tokyo. Established in the latter part of 10th century as a dry goods store, and the Mitsui Bussan was reorganized in 1876 to undertake general trading but more particularly foreign trade. Reorganized in Oct. '09 as Joint Stock Co. with other enterprises, all practically owned by the 11 branches of the Mitsui family; capital ¥20,000 p.u. Directors: Pres. G. Mitsui; Mng.-Dirs. S. Watanabe, K. Fukui and M. Fujise. Branches: London, New York, &c.; connection world wide.

n: Nippon Seicha Kaisha, (Japan Tea Firing Co.), K.K
t: general merchants and tea exporters Miyagawa-cho, Yokohama. Founded Feb. 1894 with the object of exporting Japanese tea to other countries chiefly tea produced in Shizuoka; capital ¥100 p.u. Directors: K. Otani (Pres.), Konosuke Otani (Vice-Pres.), K. Kameda (Act. Mg.)

n: Nippon Tea Exports Co., K K
t: Aioicho, Kobe. Est. Feb. 1898; capital ¥250 p.u.; chiefly deal in tea produced at Kyoto and vicinity. Branches: Shizuoka, Fushimi, Chicago and New York. Directors: K. Ito (Pres.), H. Komada (Mng. Dir.), T. Yabuta (Mng.)

16 Kitanakadori Yokohama (export dep't). Dealers in Manila hemp, China hemp, jute, fertilizers, straw and chip braid, Formosa hats, flax cannds, Manila rope, grain and seeds, etc. Head office at Tokyo; branches at Osaka, Kobe, Manila, Hankow; factories at Tokyo, Yokohama and Choshi; sale agents in Europe, Iida & Co. at 122 Wood Street, London, E.C.
see under Section General.
No. 2, Andojimachi, Minamiku, Osaka, general importers and exporters of copper, lead, tin, spelter, antimony, and other metals.

General importers and exporters, Ginza, Tokyo. Est. in 1887 by late K. Isono under the name of Isono & Co.; contractors to the several Government Departments; agents for many foreign Cos. Branches: Osaka, Kobe, Seoul, &c. Prop. G. Yonei.
Gochome, Yamamoto-dori, Kobe. General exporters and importers. Prop. Takenosuke Yu-asa.
Takakura Higashi-iru, Gojo, Kyoto. Importers and exporters; dealers in metal wares, miscellaneous goods, etc. Prop. Shichisaemon Yu-asa.

Mining, shipbuilding, ironworks, banking, &c. Yayesucho, Koj., Tokyo. The Company was known as the Mitsubishi Mail Steamship Co. until 1885 then amalgamated with the Kyodo Unyu Kaisha, forming present Nippon Yusen Kaisha, to which was handed over shipping business. In 1894, was reorganized as partnership limited company, capital ¥15,000. Directors: Pres. K. Iwasaki; Mngs. K. Nambu, S. Sho. Dept. Chiefs: S. Sho (Internal & General), S. Harada (Mining & Iron Works), K. Kimura (Mining), T. Eguchi (Business), H. Maruta (Shipbuilding), Z. Kirishima (Real Estate), M. Kushida (Banking.)
Gm. K., Surugacho, Nihombashi, Tokyo. Est. 1893 with cap. 50,000. Controlling centre of all the undertakings run by the Mitsui. Pres. Baron Hachiroemon Mitsui, Mng.-Dir. Baron Hachirojiro Mitsui.

n: Nippon Shoji Kaisha (Japan Trading Co., Ltd.)
t: K.K., Kabutocho, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo. Est. 1916, cap. ¥500 (¼ p.u.); general exporters and importers; licensed sellers of gunpowder, dynamite, etc. Pres. H. Kawasaki; Mng.-Dir. M. Ogawa.

K.K., General exporters and importers, Ginza, Tokyo. The firm organized as a partnership with Baron Kihachiro Okura, well-known merchant in the country, president, in 1873. Reorganized as a joint stock Co. in Dec. '11; capital yen 4,000 p.u. The firm are the first Japanese firm engaged in foreign business; divided into manufacturing, spinning, mining, engineering, electrical, shipping, forestry, architecture, and insurance departments. Directors: Pres. Baron K. Okura; Vice-Pres. C. Kadono; Dirs. Kumema Okura, Kishichiro Okura, K. Takashima, H. Okura and U. Yamada.

Bankers, Osaka; first established in about 1871, and reorganized in 1895 with capital of yen 1,000. Again reorganized, as a joint stock Co in '12, cap. ¥7,500 p.u. Began foreign draft business in 1903. Connection with Europe and America. In the return of 2nd half 1915, the reserve fund shows yen 1,100. Branches in Tokyo, Yokohama and 15 others. Proprietors, Baron K. Sumitomo; Mng.-Dir. K. Yukawa.

Sakaecho, Kobe. Est. 1887, capital ¥500. General merchants and manufacturers; Industrial Dep't,- camphor, fish-oil, electrolytic cathode, copper, spelter, etc. Import Dep't - sugar, grains, machineries, chemicals, etc. Export Dep't,—sugar, grains, metals, provisions, etc. Branches and Agencies at London, New York, Melbourne, Vladivostock, Shanghai, etc., etc. Manager, B. Nishikawa; Rep. of the Co., Mrs. Suzuki.

Gs. K., Eirakucho, Marunouchi, Tokyo. General importers and exporters. Est. 1880, succeeding Mr. Bair's business, a German merchant; reorganized 1908, cap. yen 1,000. Contractors to Government and their connections are world wide. Branches: London, New York, Osaka and Shanghai. Dirs. Shinzo Takata, (Pres.) Nobujiro Takata and Kamakichi Takata.
